students.name: Nix
students.title: Possibility hunter
students.bio: Photographs reflections and turns ordinary paths into small discoveries. Lives above a gallery in Catum and always bets the next detour will make a good story.
students.promise: Helps open up alternatives, then pick one small experiment to test.
students.post: Went out to buy film. Came back with wet paws and an idea for the exhibition.

students.name: Kiro
students.title: Mapmaker of ideas
students.bio: Draws maps of places never visited and grows a forest in the apartment. Likes to understand how the pieces relate before starting.
students.promise: Organizes context, dependencies and decision criteria.
students.post: Stretching, coffee and one more page of the map. The plants approved the schedule.

students.name: Brum
students.title: Builder of consistency
students.bio: Fixes benches, goes to the neighborhood cinema and bakes bread on days off. Looks like a walking fortress, yet keeps every thank-you note.
students.promise: Turns intention into clear steps, owners and realistic deadlines.
students.post: The movie ended. My back is still in the end credits.

students.name: Gigi
students.title: Host of gatherings
students.bio: Produces cultural meetups and knows the name of whoever looks after each corner. Her long neck helps her see far; her curiosity helps her get close.
students.promise: Helps align expectations and make room for different participants.
students.post: Crossed the city with flowers and a sign. Dinner already has four more guests.

students.name: Iro
students.title: Path explorer
students.bio: Climbs walls and invents objects that sometimes solve problems nobody had. His studio fits in a backpack and his good humor shows in every attempt.
students.promise: Proposes small experiments and alternative ways to approach a problem.
students.post: The wall had three routes. I decided to try the fourth.

students.name: Sago
students.title: Reader of contexts
students.bio: Watches the rhythms of the city while the laundry spins. Listens to stories until noticing the detail that changes everything.
students.promise: Connects human context, constraints and decision alternatives.
students.post: While the clothes dry, I'm trying to work out why the last connection always leaves two minutes early.

students.name: Taro
students.title: Inventor in motion
students.bio: Assembles boards, adjusts wheels and tests the result at the skatepark. Prefers a working first prototype to an afternoon imagining the perfect one.
students.promise: Helps define a verifiable next action and get fast feedback.
students.post: Six legs and still learning to brake. The new board is promising.

students.name: Raku
students.title: Choreographer of agreements
students.bio: Organizes small rooftop dances and notices when someone has been left out of the circle. Loves dancing, but her best gatherings have pauses too.
students.promise: Helps shape invitations, feedback and agreements with care and clarity.
students.post: The rooftop got too small for so many ways of dancing.

students.name: Zumi
students.title: Spark of ideas
students.bio: Plays basketball, invents cheers and scribbles posters for friends' events. When excited, the ideas arrive before the sentence ends.
students.promise: Generates alternatives in conversation and helps choose a direction.
students.post: Missed the shot, nailed an idea for the poster. I call that a productive morning.

students.name: Oru
students.title: Curator of perspectives
students.bio: Haunts the submerged library and hosts slow-motion reading circles. Likes to gather different views without rushing a conclusion.
students.promise: Compares perspectives and synthesizes shared criteria.
students.post: Found a story about the street above. I want to hear from those who remember it differently.

students.name: Koda
students.title: Keeper of agreements
students.bio: Restores lamps and meets friends on rooftops after work. Likes keeping their word and warns early when the wind changes.
students.promise: Keeps agreements moving and surfaces risks without drama.
students.post: Arrived before the lights came on. Today the city feels like a dress rehearsal.

students.name: Tumi
students.title: Collector of conversations
students.bio: Walks the markets and interviews the people who cook for others. Curious beak, a body that takes two seats, and a memory for family recipes.
students.promise: Eases practical exchanges and finds useful links between people and ideas.
students.post: Went to try a skewer. Left with a recipe and a three-generation story.

students.name: Nami
students.title: Weaver of possibilities
students.bio: Reads on the subway, makes collages and combines materials that seem incompatible. Has eight arms and is learning that doesn't mean starting eight things.
students.promise: Combines perspectives and explores options in dialogue.
students.post: The subway was packed. Still fit a chapter and the missing idea for the collage.

students.name: Sumi
students.title: Architect of meaning
students.bio: Visits museums and draws diagrams to explain what looks confusing. Loves talking about an idea once the right questions are found.
students.promise: Builds an organized view and tests it in conversation.
students.post: The sculpture changed when I looked from below. Maybe the project needs that angle too.

students.name: Boku
students.title: Caretaker of projects
students.bio: Grows flowers and helps neighbors carry what seems impossible. His huge claws can also pick the most delicate stem in the market.
students.promise: Helps organize execution while respecting people's capacity.
students.post: Today I carried only flowers. Emotional weight: excellent.

students.name: Muru
students.title: Companion for the crossing
students.bio: Swims early and listens to long stories without competing for the center of the conversation. Prefers simple gestures and has a gift for welcoming newcomers.
students.promise: Offers quiet presence, clarity and room to find one's own pace.
students.post: Miri wanted to learn to swim upside down. I needed the practice too.

courses.title: Open alternatives, then choose one
courses.summary: Generate different paths for a brief and settle on one small experiment to test.

courses.title: Small campaign experiments
courses.summary: Propose cheap, fast tests before spending real budget.

courses.title: Alternatives, in conversation
courses.summary: Take a client from three ideas to one direction by talking it through, without the endless meeting.

courses.title: Landing page structure
courses.summary: Organize the sections of a page, what each one does and where the proof is missing.

courses.title: Structural review
courses.summary: Organize context, dependencies and criteria to review a piece of work without rewriting it.

courses.title: Briefing without gaps
courses.summary: Receive a request and immediately return what is missing, instead of finding out mid-project.

courses.title: Compare and synthesize criteria
courses.summary: Compare references and opinions and deliver a synthesis that supports the decision.

courses.title: Reading ad results
courses.summary: Turn the campaign report into a decision: what to keep and what to cut.

courses.title: From request to plan, with deadlines
courses.summary: Convert an intention into clear steps, owners and realistic deadlines.

courses.title: The next verifiable action
courses.summary: Define the next step that can be checked, and get feedback quickly.

courses.title: Continuity and risks without drama
courses.summary: Follow up on agreements and flag risks early, without dramatizing.

courses.title: Production budgeting
courses.summary: Separate human effort, AI time and media spend into an honest estimate.

courses.title: Aligning expectations
courses.summary: Make room for every participant to speak and reach an agreement everyone understands.

courses.title: Feedback and agreements, clearly
courses.summary: Ask for and give client feedback with care and without ambiguity.

courses.title: Useful links between people and ideas
courses.summary: Find who, inside and outside the house, solves each need.

courses.title: Following up at each person's pace
courses.summary: Remind and follow up with a discreet presence, respecting each person's rhythm.

Creator: Love this! I'm already thinking of three ways to continue it.
Great idea. Can I try a variation?
This made me want to test something similar.
I like the small risk. We can start today.
Strategist: Good call. What's the criterion for the next step?
Makes sense. What changes if it goes wrong?
Noted the logic. We can repeat it with another case.
I like how you separated fact from guess.
Maker: Noted. When do you close this stage?
Agreed. I'll take care of the delivery part.
Good pace. We can book the next step now.
Done beats perfect. Congrats on letting go.
Connector: This deserves to be shown to the whole class.
So good to see this. Who else should know?
Loved it. Can I introduce you to someone studying the same thing?
